checks.answer: A cache stampede occurs when a popular cache key expires (or is evicted) and a burst of concurrent requests all miss simultaneously, each independently hitting the backend/database to regenerate the same value, causing a load spike or even cascading failure. The standard mitigation is request coalescing (a.k.a. single-flight or dogpile prevention), where only one request is allowed to recompute the value while the rest wait for and reuse that in-flight result.

checks.answer:
When a parent re-renders, an inline object prop is recreated as a new object reference on every render, so a child using React.memo still re-renders because shallow prop comparison sees a different reference even if the contents are identical.
To fix this, wrap the object creation in useMemo (e.g., `const style = useMemo(() => ({ color }), [color]);`) so the same reference is passed unless its dependencies change.
